question: Can a gradient-boosting model on compact image features beat a pixel-based neural-network stand-in for the paper's ResNet50 on a public image set with repeated subjects, when the test split is kept within the same subjects?
method: Stratified within-subject split; standardised pixel MLP baseline vs LightGBM with balanced class weights on HOG-style gradient-orientation features; 3-fold stratified CV on the training split for tuning; test set used once per seed.
baseline: Standardised pixel MLPClassifier (stand-in for the paper's ResNet50); tuned over alpha and hidden layer size.
improved: LightGBM classifier with class_weight='balanced' on HOG-style cell orientation histograms; tuned over n_estimators and num_leaves.
notes: Olivetti faces is a stand-in for the paper's orange images (no public orange-Brix dataset with a download link); faces are not oranges and the task is 40-way identity recognition, not sweetness regression. The MLP is not ResNet50. The test split has only about 120 images, so accuracy differences of a few points are within noise; std is over three model seeds only, with one data split. HOG-style features are a simplified numpy implementation, not skimage HOG.
